tool_arguments.query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue growth drivers fiscal 2025 Q3

events.content: NVIDIA Data Center revenue growth drivers fiscal 2025 Q3

**NVIDIA’s Data Center revenue reached a record $30.8 billion in Q3 FY2025** (quarter ended October 27, 2024), growing **17% sequentially and 112% year over year**. [[1]] 

The principal driver was **exceptional demand for the Hopper platform**, particularly the H200: H200 sales rose sequentially to **double-digit billions of dollars**, which NVIDIA described as the fastest product ramp in its history. [[2]]

**Hyperscale cloud-service providers (CSPs)** were the largest demand source, representing approximately **half of Data Center sales**; their revenue more than doubled year over year as they deployed H200 compute and high-speed networking for expanding AI-training and inference capacity. [[2]] [[3]] 

NVIDIA also benefited from broadening cloud demand beyond the largest hyperscalers: **GPU regional-cloud revenue doubled year over year**, with strength across North America, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific, including sovereign-cloud buildouts. [[2]]

**Consumer-internet companies more than doubled their NVIDIA-related spending year over year** as they scaled Hopper infrastructure, while enterprises increasingly deployed NVIDIA AI platforms for copilots and agents. [[2]] 

The growth mix extended beyond GPUs: **Spectrum-X Ethernet revenue increased more than threefold year over year**, and software, service, and support revenue was annualizing at **$1.5 billion**, supporting the broader AI-system and networking opportunity. [[2]] 

Finally, cloud availability helped translate demand into deployments: H200-powered instances were available through AWS, CoreWeave, and Microsoft Azure, with Google Cloud and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure expected to follow. [[1]] [[2]] 

In short, Q3 FY2025 Data Center growth was driven by the H200 ramp, hyperscaler AI infrastructure investment, regional/sovereign cloud expansion, accelerating inference and enterprise-AI usage, and increasing attach of networking and software/services. [[2]]

Sources:
[S3.1] NVIDIA Corporation - NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Third Quarter Fiscal 2025 — https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2024/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-Third-Quarter-Fiscal-2025/default.aspx

tool_arguments.query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue growth drivers fiscal 2025 Q4

events.content: NVIDIA Data Center revenue growth drivers fiscal 2025 Q4

**NVIDIA’s Data Center revenue reached $115.2 billion in FY2025** (year ended January 26, 2025), a **142% year-over-year increase** from $47.5 billion in FY2024; it was the central source of the company’s 114% total-revenue growth. [[1]] [[2]]

**Primary growth drivers**

- **Hopper accelerated-computing demand was the dominant driver.** NVIDIA said Data Center computing revenue grew **162%** year over year, principally due to Hopper-platform demand for large-language models, recommendation engines, and generative-AI applications. [[3]]
- **AI model scaling increased infrastructure requirements.** NVIDIA attributed rising Data Center-system demand to advances in accelerated computing and generative-AI models, as well as increasing model complexity and scale. [[3]]
- **Cloud-provider and enterprise AI build-outs supported volume.** NVIDIA’s products were being deployed through major cloud platforms—including AWS, CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and Oracle Cloud—to meet customer AI demand, underpinning broad-based capacity expansion. [[1]]
- **Networking was a meaningful secondary contributor.** Data Center networking revenue increased **51%** year over year, driven by Ethernet-for-AI revenue, including NVIDIA’s Spectrum-X end-to-end Ethernet platform. [[3]]
- **Blackwell began contributing late in the year.** NVIDIA started shipping production Blackwell systems in FY2025’s fourth quarter and reported billions of dollars of Blackwell AI-supercomputer sales in that initial production quarter, adding a new growth leg while Hopper remained the full-year engine. [[3]] [[4]]
- **The revenue ramp accelerated through the year.** Quarterly Data Center revenue rose from **$22.6 billion in Q1** to **$26.3 billion in Q2**, **$30.8 billion in Q3**, and **$35.6 billion in Q4**, reflecting sustained Hopper demand, continuing AI-infrastructure deployment, and the initial Blackwell ramp. [[5]] [[6]] [[7]] [[1]]

**Mix perspective:** Data Center compute generated **$102.2 billion** of FY2025 revenue, versus $39.0 billion in FY2024, and therefore accounted for the overwhelming majority of the platform’s $67.7 billion absolute revenue increase; networking supplied the remainder of the growth. [[2]] [[3]]

**Bottom line:** FY2025 Data Center growth was chiefly an AI-compute capacity cycle—hyperscalers, model builders, and enterprises buying Hopper-based systems for training and inference—with Spectrum-X networking expansion and the late-year Blackwell production ramp  …[truncated]

**Summary of NVIDIA Data‑Center Revenue (most recent fiscal year FY2025, quarterly)**  

| Period | Data‑Center Revenue | YoY Growth | QoQ Growth | Key Source |
|--------|--------------------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| Q2 FY2025 (Apr 2024) | **$26.3 B** | **+154 %** | +16 % | S1.1 |
| Q3 FY2025 (Oct 2024) | **$30.8 B** | **+112 %** | +17 % | S2.1 |
| Q4 FY2025 (Jan 2025) | **$35.6 B** | **+93 %** | +16 % | S5.1 |
| FY2025 (full year) | **$115.2 B** | **+142 %** | — | S6.1, S6.2 |

**Major growth drivers cited in the filings**

1. **Hopper‑platform demand (H200)** – the fastest product ramp in NVIDIA’s history; H200 sales rose to double‑digit billions of dollars in Q3 FY2025 and powered training and inference across cloud and enterprise workloads.  
2. **Hyperscale cloud‑service providers (CSPs)** – accounted for roughly half of Data‑Center sales; their spending more than doubled YoY as they built AI‑training and inference capacity.  
3. **Regional‑cloud and sovereign‑cloud expansion** – GPU revenue doubled YoY across North America, EMEA, and Asia‑Pacific.  
4. **Consumer‑internet and enterprise AI adoption** – consumer‑internet companies more than doubled NVIDIA‑related spending; enterprises began deploying NVIDIA AI platforms for copilots and agents.  
5. **Networking (Spectrum‑X Ethernet)** – grew >3× YoY, adding a meaningful secondary contribution to Data‑Center revenue.  
6. **Software, services, and support** – annualized at $1.5 B in Q3 FY2025, broadening the AI‑system opportunity.  
7. **Blackwell production ramp** – began late FY2025 Q4, contributing “billions of dollars” of AI‑supercomputer sales as the next‑generation platform alongside Hopper.

All figures are sourced from NVIDIA’s official earnings releases and SEC filings for the respective quarters and full fiscal year.
